name: Amapiano Dance Culture
notes: Amapiano dance culture pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). South Africa's sound of the 2010s–20s and the dance culture riding it worldwide. The honesty up front: amapiano's exact birthplace is CONTESTED — Soweto, Alexandra, Katlehong, Vosloorus and more Gauteng townships all claim it, and this pack states the contest rather than picking a winner; what's settled is that it is a GAUTENG TOWNSHIP creation (the name is Zulu/Xhosa for 'the pianos'), that the LOG DRUM bass — the rolling, hollow sub-melody — is its signature engine, and that Kabza De Small is widely crowned its king with the pioneer generation around him. The dance culture works exactly like this app's Afrobeats pack: NAMED MOVES minted by real dancers and spread through challenges — and the credit discipline transfers whole: learn the move, learn the name, learn who made it. One canonical credit is written into the tree: the GWARA GWARA, created by Durban's DJ BONGZ, which conquered the world's floors (and award-show stages) before amapiano absorbed it. Design truths: the amapiano groove is patient — long builds, late log-drum drops — so the pack trains restraint as a skill; the footwork bursts are genuinely solo-trainable; and the log drum pattern rides in this app's Rhythm Trainer.

seasons.finale: Film yourself grooving one full amapiano track — patient through the build, arriving WITH the log drum, never before it.
Film the amapiano bounce-sway for one song — unhurried, grounded, the shoulders narrating.
Film three footwork bursts dropped into the groove with clean returns — quick feet, calm face.
Learn two named amapiano moves from real SA dancers' clips, credit name and maker in your journal, film both.
Take it to a floor: an amapiano night, an African club, a groove session. Wait for the log drum with everyone else.

attributes.name: Build patience L1
attributes.test: groove through a full amapiano intro (often 60-90s) without escalating early — restraint held as a skill, not a failure of energy

attributes.name: Burst feet L1
attributes.test: three 15s footwork bursts in one track with clean drops back to the groove — quick in, calm out

nodes.name: The log drum — the engine
checkpoints: amapiano's signature is the LOG DRUM — the rolling, hollow bass melody that drops late and takes the floor with it; the pattern is in this app's Rhythm Trainer
around it: soft piano chords ('the pianos' — the name is Zulu/Xhosa), shakers whispering eighths, and space — amapiano breathes where other club music shouts
learn the drop by feel: when the log drum arrives, the whole floor changes gear together — that shared gear-change IS the culture

nodes.name: The build — patience as musicianship
checkpoints: amapiano arrangements are LONG — intros simmer for a minute or more before the log drum lands; the floor grooves small and saves itself
restraint reads as fluency: the dancer who explodes in the intro announces they can't hear the arrangement
practice the arrival: mark the log drum's entrance in three tracks and choreograph nothing except your gear-change

nodes.name: Gauteng's contested birth — told straight
checkpoints: amapiano's exact birthplace is CONTESTED — Soweto, Alexandra, Katlehong, Vosloorus and other Gauteng townships all claim it; this pack states the contest instead of picking a winner, because the contest is itself the history

what's settled: it is a GAUTENG TOWNSHIP creation of the 2010s, grown from kwaito, deep house, and jazz-touched keys — KABZA DE SMALL is widely crowned its king, with the pioneer generation around him
the sgubhu thread runs straight through: marabi to mbaqanga to kwaito to amapiano — this app's pantsula pack walks the same river upstream

nodes.name: Named moves & the credit discipline
checkpoints: amapiano dance works like Afrobeats dance: real dancers MINT named moves and challenges spread them worldwide — and the credit discipline transfers whole: learn the move, the name, and who made it
the canonical example: the GWARA GWARA, created by Durban's DJ BONGZ — it conquered global floors and award-show stages, and its maker's name should travel every time it does
when a move's maker is genuinely unknown or disputed, say that — 'credit unclear' is honest; silence is not

nodes.name: Amapiano to the world — the credit travels
checkpoints: 'amapiano to the world' became the scene's own export slogan — Lagos, London, and every festival circuit run piano sets now, and Afrobeats stars record on log drums
the direction matters the way it did for kuduro's Lisbon and ndombolo's Paris: the world amplifies what Gauteng invented — collaborations are the health, erasure is the disease
your job as a dancer abroad is small and real: when the log drum drops in a room that doesn't know, be the person who says 'this is South African'

nodes.name: The amapiano groove
checkpoints: a grounded, unhurried bounce-sway — knees soft, weight rolling side to side, shoulders narrating small — built to run for whole tracks
the groove sits BEHIND the beat, relaxed on purpose: amapiano cool is horizontal, never urgent
layer slowly: feet first, then hips agreeing, then shoulders — a groove assembled in one go collapses in minute three
mistakes: rushing on top of the beat (sit back into the pocket — the log drum will wait for you)
performing instead of grooving (amapiano floors read comfort, not effort)

nodes.name: Footwork bursts
checkpoints: quick tight footwork phrases — shuffles, crosses, heel flicks — dropped into the groove for a bar or two, then released back into the sway
the burst-and-return shape is the style's sentence structure: calm, flurry, calm — never a constant boil
the kwaito and pantsula footwork DNA is audible here; if you've walked the pantsula pack, your feet already speak the dialect

nodes.name: Gwara Gwara
nodes.origin: created by DJ Bongz (Durban) — credit travels with the move
checkpoints: the signature: one leg lifts and rotates in a lazy stir while the same-side arm winds with it — the whole body leaning into a rolling, off-balance churn
it looks loose and IS precise: the stir stays on the beat, the supporting knee stays soft, the lean never becomes a stumble
say its maker when you teach it — DJ Bongz built the move the world borrowed; the name is part of the choreography

nodes.name: The challenge shelf — learning with credit
checkpoints: the living vocabulary: amapiano mints moves continuously through challenges from South African dancers — pick two current ones and learn them from SA source clips, not from copies of copies
the log: song, move name, and the dancer you learned it from go in your journal — the same shelf discipline as the Afrobeats pack
fast absorption is the meta-skill: watch, mark, full-out inside one track — the culture moves at feed speed and rewards dancers who keep up honestly

nodes.name: The groove set — filmed
checkpoints: film one full track: patient through the build, gear-change WITH the log drum, groove carrying, two footwork bursts, Gwara Gwara and one challenge move landed
the restraint audit: did the intro stay small? early escalation fails the set even if everything after it shines
credits on camera: the township contest named, DJ Bongz named, your challenge moves' makers named

nodes.name: The groove session
checkpoints: find the floor: amapiano nights and African club sessions run worldwide now — the sound left home and took its dance culture along
the floor's etiquette is the music's: groove with the room, save yourself through the build, and change gears with everyone when the log drum says so
when the sound travels, the credit travels: amapiano is South African, from Gauteng's townships — say it whenever the room forgets
